title: Code Review and Engineering Standards knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best describes the purpose of “Code Review and Engineering Standards”?
options: Code Review and Engineering Standards helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
Code Review and Engineering Standards means the browser can enforce all permissions without the backend.
Code Review and Engineering Standards removes the need for error handling, accessibility checks and tests.
Code Review and Engineering Standards should be implemented by copying a snippet without checking the Angular version.
questions.answer_key: Code Review and Engineering Standards helps explain and implement one part of an Angular application; choose the API pattern that matches the behavior and verify it.
questions.explanation: Code Review and Engineering Standards is a concept in the supplied Angular curriculum. Its correct application depends on the intended behavior, surrounding context and verification.

questions.prompt: How should a learner work with “Code review checklists” in this lesson?
options: Treat “Code review checklists” as a reason to skip the surrounding application context.
Assume “Code review checklists” works identically across every Angular major and runtime.
Use “Code review checklists” to bypass runtime validation of external or user-provided values.
Connect “Code review checklists” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.answer_key: Connect “Code review checklists” to the lesson goal, use a focused example, and validate the behavior in the selected Angular environment.
questions.explanation: The PDF explicitly lists “Code review checklists” under Code Review and Engineering Standards. Anchor it in a small example and check the behavior rather than relying on a memorized phrase.

questions.prompt: What is the strongest verification approach for “Code Review and Engineering Standards”?
options: Treat a successful client-side render as backend authorization evidence.
Ignore a failing test if the component looks correct in one browser.
Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
Assume an SVG diagram proves the code compiled and passed tests.
questions.answer_key: Run the example in a compatible local Angular workspace, test the expected result and one failure case, and document any version limitation.
questions.explanation: Verification evidence should match the running environment. Static teaching snippets are not compiler output, and frontend checks do not replace backend authorization.
